overall_status: A useful finite-resource kernel boundary is reconstructed for an ideal continuous spatial clock. The recent apparatus is a source-reported spectroscopy demonstration, not a demonstrated stabilized or alias-free clock. The kernel theorem is internal model mathematics; no new physical capability or priority claim is established.
target: Test whether spatially gated continuous atom transport removes a measurement bottleneck after temporal response, atom flux, and a strongest zero-dead-time control are charged.

claims.exact_statement: For the ideal normalized rectangular per-atom phase response z_t=tau^{-1} integral_t^{t+tau} y(s) ds, averaging over a uniform continuum of atom start times t in [0,T-tau] gives aggregate kernel k_T(s)=|[0,T-tau] intersect [s-tau,s]|/[tau(T-tau)]. It is flat on the interior [tau,T-tau] and has boundary ramps of width tau. Its per-atom frequency response is exp(i pi f tau) sinc(pi f tau), with exact zeros at every nonzero f=k/tau.
claims.status: internally derived exact result for the stated ideal phase-averaging interface; it is not the measured Rabi sensitivity function of the apparatus
assumptions: Known constant transit time tau and uniform spatial/temporal atom-start density over the stated interval.
Linearized phase response is a rectangular average; actual Rabi excitation probabilities, velocity spread, spatial magnetic-field profile, and contrast inhomogeneity are not included.
Atom outcomes are combined with equal weights for the aggregate-kernel formula.
claims.novelty_boundary: Rectangular-window Fourier zeros and Fubini aggregation are elementary model consequences, not a claim of novel metrology. The contribution is a scoped boundary against inferring alias-free readout from continuous delivery alone.
costs: Transit time tau=L/v and its calibration uncertainty.
Atom flux, arrival-time/occupancy record, and edge handling over the measurement interval.
Empirical Rabi sensitivity-function identification, LO-noise PSD, contrast, and state/readout noise.
claims.physical_falsifier: For the actual moving-lattice apparatus, measure the complex response to weak LO frequency-modulation tones. A response incompatible with the measured per-atom sensitivity function or absence of its predicted conditioning/null structure refutes transfer of the rectangular model; it does not refute the aggregate-kernel identity.
claims.next_gate: Measure the actual atom-resolved sensitivity function and repeat the transfer-function experiment with a matched, gapless two-ensemble interleaved clock at the same isotope, LO, interrogation time, total atom flux, contrast, and readout.

claims.exact_statement: For a stationary Poisson stream of atoms entering a zone with dwell time tau at rate r, the in-zone occupancy at a fixed interior time is Poisson(r tau), so the empty-zone probability is exp(-r tau) and occupancy coefficient of variation is 1/sqrt(r tau). The expected number of arrival gaps longer than tau across duration T is approximately r T exp(-r tau), up to boundary effects; this is a Markov bound on the probability of any such uncovered interval.
claims.status: internally derived exact Poisson occupancy result plus a long-record expected-gap approximation; Poisson arrivals are not asserted for the published lattice conveyor
assumptions: Stationary homogeneous Poisson arrival process, independent of the LO and atom outcome noise.
Each atom contributes sensitivity on exactly one interval of length tau.
Long-record gap-rate approximation ignores start/end correction terms.
claims.novelty_boundary: The occupancy identities are standard Poisson-process consequences. They show that mean continuous delivery does not by itself guarantee gap-free or uniform sensitivity under a stochastic arrival model.
costs: Required flux depends logarithmically on total observation time and desired gap probability.
No-gap coverage and pointwise sensitivity flatness are different constraints; at r tau=18, pointwise occupancy CV is about 24%.
Empirical arrival Fano factor and spatial occupancy must be measured before using the Poisson model.
claims.physical_falsifier: Time-tag atom arrivals/occupancy. A non-Poisson record outside the assumed model invalidates its numerical gap bound; an observed gap rate materially above r T exp(-r tau) after boundary correction falsifies the stated Poisson approximation.
claims.next_gate: Obtain the source's atom arrival/occupancy record and evaluate the measured sensitivity-weighted coverage, not merely the mean loading rate.

claims.exact_statement: In an ideal independent-atom mid-fringe phase readout with contrast C, per-atom interrogation duration tau, and N detections, frequency Fisher information is 4 pi^2 C^2 tau^2 N, yielding sd(nu_hat) >= 1/(2 pi C tau sqrt(N)). A spatial conveyor and a gapless interleaved two-ensemble clock with equal N, tau, C, per-atom response kernel, and readout noise have identical QPN/readout floors in this model.
claims.status: internally derived benchmark model; not an observed clock stability or an exact formula for the source's Rabi line
assumptions: Ideal local mid-fringe phase likelihood with independent Bernoulli outcomes.
Known contrast C, calibrated interrogation time tau, and identical effective phase kernels across architectures.
Equal total detected atoms N and equal total averaging time; LO noise and dead-time costs must be compared separately.
claims.novelty_boundary: The QPN formula is standard. It denies an automatic precision gain from continuous transport against a strongest already gapless interleaved control; spatial transport may still improve hardware throughput or synchronization overhead.
costs: Atoms per second and total detected atoms.
Per-atom clock exposure tau and total atom-time N tau.
Contrast, atom preparation and readout photons, laser/transport/magnetic-field power, LO PSD, and calibration uncertainty.
claims.physical_falsifier: At equal atom flux, duration, interrogation response, and readout, a reproducible Allan-deviation advantage over the two-ensemble control would falsify the equal-resource no-automatic-gain conclusion's physical transfer; a null difference supports architecture-only benefit within that tested band.
claims.next_gate: Run both clock architectures on the same LO with matched total Sr atoms, measured transit/readout costs, injected common LO spectrum, and preregistered Allan-deviation bands.

claims.exact_statement: Under tau=0.75 s, r=24 s^-1, T=86400 s, and C=1, a Poisson arrival fixture has mean in-zone occupancy 18, fixed-time empty probability exp(-18), expected long-gap count scale 0.032/day, occupancy CV 23.6%, N=2,073,600, ideal mid-fringe QPN/readout frequency SD about 0.147 mHz, and first rectangular-kernel zero 1.33 Hz.
claims.status: reproducible illustrative calculation; none of these flux/noise figures is reported for the spatial-clock apparatus
assumptions: Uses the stated ideal Poisson and mid-fringe phase models.
claims.novelty_boundary: A feasibility-scale calculation only; it is not a source-data replay, engineered design, or instrument prediction.
costs: Flux 24 atoms/s; 18 atoms simultaneously in the 0.75-s zone; 2,073,600 detected atoms per day; contrast assumed unity.
claims.physical_falsifier: Measured flux, contrast, atom correlations, or LO/readout spectra that differ from the illustrative assumptions make the numerical prediction inapplicable.
claims.next_gate: Replace every fixture value with measured values and include preparation/readout throughput, transport energy, calibration uncertainty, and LO PSD.

source_boundary.primary_spatial_platform: Nishida et al., Nature Communications 17, 7662 (2026), https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-026-76017-1. Source-reported 88Sr moving-lattice transport at 16 mm/s through a 12-mm interaction region, localized magnetic clock coupling, and a 1.2-Hz-wide spectrum. This is spectroscopy and continuous delivery, not a demonstrated stabilized clock or measured alias-free Allan deviation.
source_boundary.strong_control_prior_art: Zero-Dead-Time Strontium Lattice Clock with a Stability at 10^-19 Level, Phys. Rev. Lett. (2026), DOI 10.1103/zbpb-6qxb; source-reported interleaved ensembles and 2.9e-19 at 20,000 s. It is a strong architecture control but a different isotope/device, so it is not an equal-resource same-apparatus trial.
source_boundary.external_validation: No independent replication or specialist review.
